title: United Republic of Tanzania Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
temporal_coverage: Current climate-risk exposure and climate-development scenarios through 2050, reported in 2024
methodology: CCDR executive summary reports macroeconomic, climate, sectoral, institutional and financial modeling under climate and growth scenarios.
limitations: Summary-level results are modeled and scenario-dependent; detailed methods are outside this executive summary.

title: Tanzania's Nationally Determined Contribution
organization: United Republic of Tanzania, Vice President's Office (Union and Environment)
temporal_coverage: Observed climate through 2016 and projections through 2090 reported in the 2021 NDC
methodology: NDC draws on the Second National Communication, national adaptation planning and cited Future Climate for Africa projections.
limitations: NDC reports results from earlier studies; its climate-risk assessment methods were still to be developed when submitted.

title: Performance Audit Report on the Management of Floods
organization: National Audit Office of Tanzania, Controller and Auditor General
temporal_coverage: Flood-management audit covering 2020/21-2023/24; includes field observations and cited event reports from 2023-2024.
methodology: Government performance audit combining interviews, records review and physical site observations in selected flood-prone local authorities.
limitations: Visited local authorities were selected for flood exposure; results are not a representative survey of all councils.

title: Water Sector Development Programme Phase III: Annual Water Sector Status Report 2024
organization: United Republic of Tanzania, Ministry of Water
temporal_coverage: Water-resource, rainfall and service delivery reporting for 2024, published March 2025.
methodology: Annual ministry reporting on hydrology, water services, programme performance and implementation constraints.
limitations: Annual basin and station summaries do not establish anthropogenic climate attribution or household-level impacts.

title: Perceived existence of farmer-pastoralist conflicts in relation to climate change in Kilosa District, Tanzania
organization: Emmanuel E. Chingonikaya and Farida Salehe; published by AkiNik Publications and hosted in the Sokoine University of Agriculture Institutional Repository
temporal_coverage: 2021 cross-sectional study of farmer-pastoralist relations in selected Kilosa wards and villages.
methodology: Repository abstract reports a cross-sectional design with 120 respondents, household surveys, focus groups and key-informant interviews.
limitations: Only the repository abstract was readable; no causal identification, conflict prevalence or ward-level results were available.

title: Local governance and climate change adaptation: evidence from Monduli and Longido districts, Tanzania
organization: Maeda, Namwata and Kumburu; Moshi Co-operative University Institutional Repository
temporal_coverage: 2025 mixed-methods study of local-authority adaptation implementation; study fieldwork dates not stated in the abstract.
methodology: Repository abstract reports a 351-member committee survey, 20 key-informant interviews and six focus groups.
limitations: The full article PDF timed out; the abstract supplies no district-specific estimates or detailed measurement definitions.

title: Climate adaptation in Tanzania's national budgeting process: embedding flood and drought preparedness
organization: London School of Economics Grantham Research Institute and Behavioural Adaptation for Water Security and Inclusion project partners
temporal_coverage: Eight-page August 2026 policy brief using 2025 interviews and national budget-cycle analysis.
methodology: Multi-actor behaviour-journey analysis drawing on 43 purposively selected 2025 government and non-government interviews.
limitations: National budgeting analysis, not a district impact evaluation; some budget shares are attributed to cited external reports.

title: Enhancing the Adaptive Capacity of Semi-Arid Agropastoral Communities through Local Adaptation Plans in Dodoma
organization: IKI Small Grants programme; implemented by the Forum on Climate Change (FORUMCC)
temporal_coverage: Completed project page for July 2023-August 2025; reports district planning and engagement outputs.
methodology: Grant-programme page summarizes project context, implementation locations and implementer-reported outputs.
limitations: Project-reported outputs and engagement; approved funding is not evidence of expenditure or independently evaluated impact.
